summary: AE + SE from Redwood scoped a 2-3 week POC with MedPath focused on quality evaluation for clinical summarization and triage tasks. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination bounds, formatting), workload sizing (QPS, tokens per request, peak concurrency), benchmark plan (replay vs synthetic, metrics) and timeline. Agreement to share golden prompts, baseline notebook, and schedule a hands-on benchmarking slot.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lisa Park (CTO, MedPath), Ravi Patel (Head of ML Ops, MedPath), Sofia Martinez (PM, MedPath)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's a busy week. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Dr. Lisa Park (MedPath): Hi, Lisa here.
[00:08] Ravi (MedPath): Ravi on the line.
[00:10] Sofia (MedPath): Sofia here.
[00:12] Ben (Redwood): Ben here, SE, ready to dig into the quality plan.
[00:18] Maya (Redwood): Cool. Objective today is to align on success criteria for the POC, get sizing numbers so we can build a representative benchmark, and agree on the quality eval plan - golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach.
[00:35] Sofia (MedPath): For context, our use case is clinical note summarization and triage suggestions. We want to make sure the model doesn't hallucinate diagnoses, keeps the format strict for downstream systems, and hits throughput targets.
[01:02] Ben (Redwood): Got it. Two separate axes: quality (accuracy, hallucination, structured format) and infra (latency, throughput, cost). We'll propose a scoring rubric that combines automated metrics plus human adjudication.
[01:20] Ravi (MedPath): Our current traffic: average 12 QPS, peak 65 QPS during morning batch, median tokens per request ~450, worst case up to 1,200 tokens for full note. Retention and PHI is a concern - we'll share a redacted sample dataset.
[01:42] Maya (Redwood): Perfect, that helps. For the POC we recommend two parallel tracks: 1) quality eval on a representative sample (golden prompts + curated cases) and 2) load/latency benchmarks on replayed traffic to validate p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
[02:05] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): Timeline? We were hoping to get something in two weeks.
[02:09] Maya (Redwood): Two to three weeks is doable. Week 1: data share + golden prompt curation. Week 2: run automated regressions and small human evals. Week 3 (optional): full load benchmark and finalize report.
[02:30] Ben (Redwood): On the quality eval, our suggested components: golden prompts (10-30 canonical prompts per task), regression test set (~200 examples), hallucination checks (entity hallucination, fabricated medications/diagnoses), formatting/structure checks (JSON schema, required fields), and scoring approach.
[02:58] Sofia (MedPath): Can you expand on scoring? What are we looking at?
[03:02] Ben (Redwood): Sure. Automated scoring: exact match / token overlap for structured fields, F1 for entity extraction, string similarity for free-text summary (we avoid relying on BLEU/ROUGE alone). For hallucination we run an entity-verification pass: check generated entities against the input and external knowledge lists, flag ungrounded entities. Then weighted scoring: e.g., 50% clinical correctness (entities & assertions), 20% hallucination penalty, 20% formatting/valid output, 10% latency/cost if you want to fold infra.
[03:40] Ravi (MedPath): We care most about hallucinations and correctness - even if slower, wrong outputs are worse.
[03:48] Maya (Redwood): Noted. We'll make hallucination a hard cutoff for fail cases and report continuous metrics. For pass/fail we can set thresholds - for example: <3% hallucination rate on regression set, >92% entity recall for key fields, and valid JSON schema 99% of the time. Those are starting points - you can tighten them.
[04:18] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): That sounds reasonable. How do you detect hallucinations reliably?
[04:25] Ben (Redwood): We use a combination: simple heuristics (does the model invent a medication not mentioned?), cross-check against the source note, and sample human adjudication to estimate false positive/false negative rates. For common entities we can use a lexicon; for more complex assertions we'll rely on human review on a stratified sample.
[04:48] Maya (Redwood): Also we'll include format checks: validate JSON schema, required fields present, field lengths, enumerated values. If format fails, we can short-circuit downstream ingestion.
[05:05] Sofia (MedPath): Regression tests - how large and how do we pick examples?
[05:09] Ben (Redwood): We recommend ~200 examples for automated regression, selected to cover edge cases: long notes, ambiguous language, uncommon medications, multiple comorbidities, and some adversarial prompts where hallucination risk is higher. Golden prompts are the canonical prompts with expected outputs for about 20-30 high-value examples for human eval.
[05:40] Ravi (MedPath): For load testing, can Redwood run it in our VPC or do you prefer hosted? We have firewall rules and prefer run-in-place for PHI.
[05:50] Maya (Redwood): For the POC, Private deployment or a dedicated pool with VPC peering is possible. For initial quality evals we can work with de-identified data in hosted, but for full load test we should do VPC peering or an on-prem bundle. We'll send options in writing.
[06:10] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): Cost estimate? Rough ballpark for dedicated.
[06:14] Maya (Redwood): We'll produce a ballpark based on your QPS and token profile. Expect dedicated pool pricing +/- depending on reserved capacity. We'll include cost per 1M tokens and estimated monthly cost for baseline traffic in the POC deliverable.
[06:32] Ben (Redwood): Back to scoring - human eval: we propose 3 reviewers per golden prompt for majority vote on correctness and hallucination. Also a small blind A/B between candidate model and current baseline to quantify regressions and improvements.
[06:52] Sofia (MedPath): What's the baseline? We're currently using an internal LLM + heuristics - variable performance.
[06:58] Maya (Redwood): We'll run both models on the same regression set and produce side-by-side metrics. For hallucination we give both continuous rates and examples.
[07:12] Ravi (MedPath): Any tooling you recommend for annotation?
[07:15] Ben (Redwood): We can provide a simple annotation spreadsheet and a small web UI for adjudication. We'll share the baseline eval notebook that computes metrics so your team can reproduce.
[07:30] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): For confidentiality, we need KMS and audit logs.
[07:34] Maya (Redwood): Yes - we'll include KMS/HSM options, per-request audit logs, and SOC2/ISO docs in the security pack.
[07:45] Ben (Redwood): On regression cadence - after initial run, we recommend a weekly regression check for the pilot to catch drift after model/ prompt changes.
[07:55] Sofia (MedPath): What about hallucination threshold selection? We want conservative thresholds.
[07:59] Maya (Redwood): We can set conservative defaults for POC: hallucination failure if >2% on golden set, but operational thresholds can be tightened post-POC. We'll show sensitivity analysis in the report.
[08:15] Ravi (MedPath): Are you going to test different quantization or model variants?
[08:19] Ben (Redwood): Yes - we typically test 3 variants: highest-accuracy baseline, a quantized performance variant, and a cost-optimized variant. We'll include regression curves for each so you can trade cost vs quality.
[08:34] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): Format enforcement - can the model output strict JSON? We need downstream ingestion to not break.
[08:40] Ben (Redwood): We'll validate against schema and treat schema failures as errors. We also recommend temperature/penalty settings and prompt-engineering patterns that anchor the model to the schema - we'll include golden prompt templates.
[08:56] Maya (Redwood): Benchmark plan summary: 1) ingest your redacted sample set, 2) run automated regression on ~200 examples, 3) human adjudication on 20-30 golden prompts, 4) run load replay for p50/p95/p99 with a representative QPS profile.
[09:18] Sofia (MedPath): What's the expected runtime for the full benchmark?
[09:21] Ben (Redwood): Automated regressions are a couple hours; human adjudication depends on reviewers but usually 2-3 days of work for 3 reviewers full-time if needed, but we can do a smaller sample for the POC. Load replay depends on scale - we'll need a 2-hour sustained test at peak for reliable p99.
[09:42] Maya (Redwood): Proposed POC milestones: Day 0-3: data share + kickoff; Day 4-8: golden prompts & automated regression; Day 9-12: human eval + initial report; Day 13-15: load benchmark + final report.
[10:05] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): That map looks good. Any blockers we should know about?
[10:09] Ravi (MedPath): Internal security review might add a few days; we need Redwood's SOC2 docs and KMS detail to clear infra. Also need a redaction script for PHI to produce test data.
[10:24] Maya (Redwood): We'll send SOC2 package and KMS options today, and Ben will provide the eval notebook and a redaction checklist.
[10:31] Ben (Redwood): One more note on metrics: for clinical correctness we'll surface false positive rate for high-severity assertions as a separate stat - e.g., fabricated diagnoses/meds.
[10:45] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): Can you example what a hallucination report looks like?
[10:49] Ben (Redwood): Short example: input note -> model output (diagnosis X) -> evidence check (not present in note) -> label: hallucination; include supporting lines and adjudicator comment. We'll include sample report in the notebook.
[11:05] Maya (Redwood): Ok let's recap next steps.
[11:08] Maya (Redwood): Action items: we'll send security docs (SOC2), Ben will package golden prompts and baseline notebook, MedPath will provide redacted sample and QPS profile, and we'll schedule the 2-hour benchmark.
[11:20] Sofia (MedPath): Sounds good. Please include cost estimate for a dedicated pool.
[11:23] Maya (Redwood): Will do.
[11:26] Dr. Lisa (MedPath): Thanks all, excited to get started.
[11:30] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links and the file attachments.
[11:36] End of recording. Note: transcription has occasional mislabels and homophones (K-V cash for KV cache, Redwood-verify mentioned once).
